haiku-low.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine's invoices go only to the shadow store, and it never charges or writes the ledger.
haiku-low.q2: The new engine computes, charges and writes the ledger. The old engine keeps computing every invoice into the shadow store without charging.
haiku-low.q3: 7 consecutive UTC days with completed nightly comparisons and mismatch rate below 0.1%, plus at least 5,000 invoices compared. A person makes the move with an audited write.
haiku-low.q4: On-call manual rollback, or an automatic trigger when new-engine charge failures exceed 2% in a 10-minute window. Automatic applies in both or new_only, the latter only before day 35.
haiku-low.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only and resets the gates. The rollout must then go through shadow again, and the 7-day count starts over.
haiku-low.q6: After day 35 in new_only, because the usage event log keeps only 35 days. Skipped events age out from the oldest forward, so the practical deadline is earlier.
haiku-low.q7: Workers read billing_mode at the start of every run. A mode change applies only to runs starting after the audited write; an invoice already in progress finishes in its old mode.
haiku-low.q8: In the rollout record in the billing store. The system checks gates when the move write arrives and refuses it if a gate is unmet or the kill switch is set.
haiku-low.q9: The rollout controller computes the failure rate from charge-path counts in the rollout record. When it exceeds 2% in a 10-minute window, it starts the rollback steps and never writes billing_mode.
haiku-low.q10: Charges that fall due are held, not dropped. They are actually made in resume_old, after on-call writes old_only and the kill switch is cleared.
haiku-low.q11: reconcile_ownership checks the provider by key. Provider success means the new engine owns the period, so it is charged nothing; the same idempotency key is reused on every retry.
haiku-low.q12: Billing stays frozen with the kill switch set. Rollback steps are idempotent, so the interrupted rollback resumes at its last completed step.

sonnet.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine's invoices go to the shadow store only; it never charges or writes the ledger.
sonnet.q2: The new engine computes, charges and writes the ledger. The old engine keeps computing every invoice into the shadow store without charging.
sonnet.q3: 7 consecutive UTC days, each with a completed nightly comparison and mismatch rate below 0.1%, and at least 5,000 invoices compared across the 7 days. A person makes the move with an audited write.
sonnet.q4: The new engine's charge failure rate above 2% in any 10-minute window (failed/all new-engine charge attempts; windows with no attempts never trigger). It happens in both and new_only (new_only only before day 35).
sonnet.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only and resets the gates. The rollout must go through shadow again, and the 7-day count starts over.
sonnet.q6: At day 35 in new_only (decommissioning allowed on or after day 35), because the usage event log keeps only 35 days. In practice the deadline is earlier since skipped events age out from the oldest forward.
sonnet.q7: Workers read billing_mode from the config service at the start of every run. A run that started earlier finishes in its old mode; the change applies to runs that start after the audited write.
sonnet.q8: In the rollout record (daily comparison results, shadow streak, unresolved mismatches, Finance sign-off) in the billing store. The system checks the gates when the audited write arrives and refuses it if a gate is not met or the kill switch is set.
sonnet.q9: The rollout controller. It computes the rate of failed new-engine charge attempts divided by all new-engine attempts in a 10-minute window (counts written by the charge path to the rollout record). When above 2% it starts the rollback steps, without writing billing_mode.
sonnet.q10: They are held, not dropped (kill switch set; no charges by either engine's ordinary runs). They are made by the old engine in resume_old, after on-call writes old_only, once per unowned or not-yet-charged period under its key; ordinary charging resumes after the kill switch is cleared.
sonnet.q11: reconcile_ownership checks the provider by idempotency key for each period with a new-engine attempt; if the provider shows success, the new engine owns the period, the ledger entry is added if missing, and nothing is charged. The old engine charges only unowned or not-yet-charged periods, once, under the same key. Replayed owned periods are computed but not charged.
sonnet.q12: Billing stays frozen: kill switch set, no charges or ledger writes by ordinary runs, charges held, billing_mode unchanged. Each step is idempotent, so the rollback resumes at its last completed step. What happens if the controller is down is an open question.
